Vietnam’s one-party system means the relevant record here is intra-party succession and constitutional state handoff, not coalition bargaining.","evidence":[{"title":"Vietnam’s top leader Trong dies at 80, party says","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-07-19","url":"https://theprint.in/world/vietnams-top-leader-trong-dies-at-80-party-says/2181868/","summary":"Reuters reported that Trọng secured a third term in 2021 after the normal two-term limit for the party leader was waived. That is the strongest evidence against strict term-limit observance.","question_ids":["4B.8","4B.2"]},{"title":"Vietnam names acting president after legislature votes to remove Thuong","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-03-21","url":"https://theprint.in/world/vietnam-names-acting-president-after-legislature-votes-to-remove-thuong/2009559/","summary":"After President Vo Van Thuong was removed, the legislature appointed Vo Thi Anh Xuan as acting head of state until the National Assembly elected a replacement, explicitly “in accordance with Vietnam’s constitution.” This supports a formal constitutional transfer mechanism in 2024.","question_ids":["4B.8"]},{"title":"Politburo issues notice on Party General Secretary’s health","publisher":"Government of Viet Nam (English portal)","date":"2024-07-18","url":"https://en.baochinhphu.vn/politburo-issues-notice-on-party-general-secretarys-health-111240718161208612.htm","summary":"The Politburo said Trọng was working while receiving treatment and assigned Tô Lâm to be in charge of the Party Central Committee, Politburo, and Secretariat for the immediate future. This shows an orderly internal handoff, but it was a party-controlled succession, not an open transfer.","question_ids":["4B.8"]},{"title":"Vietnam President To Lam takes top job as Communist Party chief","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-08-03","url":"https://theprint.in/world/vietnam-president-to-lam-takes-top-job-as-communist-party-chief/2205833/","summary":"Reuters reported that Lam took over the duties of party chief on July 18 and was unanimously supported by party delegates on August 3. This indicates a controlled succession process, though still opaque and intra-party rather than pluralistic.","question_ids":["4B.8"]}]}
